title: Zagori & the Vikos Gorge

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (35 °C+ on the gorge floor, springs dry, vipers active); November–April (Tymfi under snow, Astraka refuge shut)

food.note: Taverna meal with wine €14–€22; refuge half-board ~€30

transport.note: Rental car 7 days €200–€300 plus fuel; a car is effectively mandatory

activities.note: Refuge night, Voidomatis raft, Anavasi maps

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — comfortable with 1,000 m climbs on rough limestone and back-to-back 20 km days; no alpinism required

gatewayAirport: IOA — Ioannina "King Pyrrhus" (45 min to Monodendri, 1 h 15 to Papingo); fallback PVK — Preveza/Aktion, 2 h 15
summary: Zagori offers two entirely different running surfaces twenty minutes apart: the shaded limestone floor of the Vikos Gorge — 900 m deep from the Oxya rim to the Voidomatis bed — and the bare karst amphitheatre of Mt Tymfi above Papingo, where a 1,000 m climb lands you at a refuge on a 1,950 m col. Linking them are forty-six stone villages joined by 18th-century mule paths and single-arch packhorse bridges. The week's arc is deliberate: two orientation days, a two-day Tymfi block with a night at altitude, a genuine recovery day on the river, then a fast village-path day and a rim finish. It suits an experienced runner who wants technical volume without glacier travel.

itinerary.title: Land at Ioannina, shake out on the Vradeto Steps
itinerary.morning: Fly into IOA, collect the car, stock up in Ioannina — Zagori shops are tiny. Drive 45 minutes to Kapesovo.
itinerary.afternoon: Shake-out down the **Skala Vradetou**, roughly 1,100 restored zigzag steps into the Mezaria ravine, up to Vradeto (1,340 m) and out to the **Beloi viewpoint** facing the gorge's north wall. Take the descent slow — first contact with polished Zagori limestone.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Sterna** in Kapesovo; order the hortopita and a Zitsa white.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km / 520 m D+ / ~70% kalderimi flagstone / 1 h 30–2 h; 45 min transfer.

itinerary.title: The full Vikos Gorge traverse
itinerary.morning: Leave Monodendri by 07:00. Drop from the **Agia Paraskevi monastery** trailhead — 450 m down in 2.5 km on the loosest ground of the week — then north-west along the dry bed on cobble, slab and beech shade.
itinerary.afternoon: Refill at the **Voidomatis springs** at Klima where the river resurfaces, then climb 250 m in 40 minutes to **Vikos village**. Pickup, or add the kalderimi link down to Aristi.
itinerary.evening: **Kanela kai Garyfallo** in Vitsa — book ahead; order the daily wild-greens dish.
itinerary.dayStats: 12.8 km / 320 m up, 690 m down / 2 h 15–3 h / no signal for 9 km / one reliable water point.

itinerary.title: Up to Astraka, the thousand-metre climb
itinerary.morning: Drive to **Mikro Papingo** (960 m) and start the O3 climb at 07:00: box scrub to the **Antalki spring**, then open karst and the traverse to the **Astraka col, 1,950 m**, where the refuge sits between Astraka and Lapatos. 1 h 45–2 h 20 with power-hiking.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop the pack, then the 45-minute out-and-back across the plateau to **Drakolimni** (2,050 m) with its alpine newts, on the lip above the Aoos gorge.
itinerary.evening: Refuge fixed menu — soup, bean stew, feta — and sunset from the terrace over the Papingo towers.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.5 km / 1,050 m D+ to the refuge, plus 5.5 km / 220 m D+ for the lake; refuge 1,950 m, 51 beds.

itinerary.title: Astraka summit ridge, then the long descent
itinerary.morning: Away by 06:45. **Astraka (2,436 m)** by the south-east flank from the col, 55–75 minutes with a short easy scramble on good rock. Strong runners add the plateau traverse to **Gamila I (2,497 m)**, +2 h.
itinerary.afternoon: Reverse the Papingo descent, 1,000 m of karst and cobble that punishes quads harder than the climb did lungs. Finish in the **Rogovo rock pools** above Megalo Papingo as an ice bath.
itinerary.evening: Grilled meats and tsipouro at Kalliopi's in Megalo Papingo, then a very early night.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km / 1,600 m D+ / 4 h 30–6 h / technicality 4 on the summit block / high point 2,436 m.

itinerary.title: Recovery day on the Voidomatis
itinerary.morning: Deliberate low day: 6 km flat on the **Voidomatis riverside path, Klidonia bridge to Aristi bridge** — packed gravel, plane-tree shade, 40 m total elevation change, conversational pace only.
itinerary.afternoon: A half-day Class II raft on the Voidomatis, or nothing at all. Drive out to the **Kokkorou** and **Plakidas (Kalogeriko)** packhorse bridges near Kipoi.
itinerary.evening: Aristi Mountain Resort restaurant — Epirot cheeses, trahana, Glinavos wine.
itinerary.dayStats: 6 km / 40 m D+ / 100% flat gravel / ~35 minutes running.

itinerary.title: The village kalderimi link
itinerary.morning: Point-to-point **Kipoi → Koukouli → Dilofo → Vitsa** on restored mule paths across three single-arch bridges. Constant short climbs, deep forest, no exposure — the fast, flowing day of the week.
itinerary.afternoon: Extend on the **Kapesovo–Tsepelovo** link if the legs are good, or drive to Tsepelovo for the short Mezaria ravine loop and coffee under the plane tree.
itinerary.evening: Tsepelovo taverna — order gida vrasti (boiled goat) if it is on the board.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km / 600 m D+ / ~50% forest singletrack, 35% kalderimi, 15% asphalt / 1 h 45–2 h 30.

itinerary.title: Rim run at Oxya, then out
itinerary.morning: Drive to the **Oxya viewpoint** above Monodendri and run the rim path north — 8 km out-and-back on pine-needle singletrack directly above the 900 m drop, seeing Day 2's route from above.
itinerary.afternoon: Pita and coffee in Monodendri, then the 45-minute drive to Ioannina; an hour in the Ottoman castle quarter if the flight allows.
itinerary.evening: Late departure from IOA, or a night on the Ioannina lakefront.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 260 m D+ / 1 h–1 h 20; 45 min drive to IOA.

accommodationStrategy.name: Archontiko Zarkada
accommodationStrategy.description: Two minutes' jog from the Agia Paraskevi gorge trailhead, so the Vikos traverse starts on foot at 07:00 without moving the car. Early breakfast on request if you ask the night before. Roughly €70–€95 double in shoulder season, with secure indoor storage for shoes and packs.

accommodationStrategy.name: Papaevangelou Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The Tymfi base: ten minutes from the Mikro Papingo trailhead, balcony view of the Astraka towers, and owners who know real-time refuge and snow conditions — worth more than any website. Ask for a 06:00 coffee flask before the summit day.

accommodationStrategy.name: Aristi Mountain Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: The recovery base. Indoor pool, sauna and massage make it the right place to sit between the Astraka block and the kalderimi day, five minutes from the Voidomatis path. €130–€200 a night — you are paying for the recovery.

logistics.connectivity: Greece is EU, so roaming is at domestic rates; Cosmote has the best Zagori coverage. Assume **no signal on the gorge floor** and patchy service on the north Tymfi plateau. Download offline maps in the village.
logistics.emergency: **112** for everything; the Hellenic Rescue Team's Epirus section covers Tymfi. Forest fire **199**. Buy insurance that explicitly covers mountain running above 2,000 m — standard policies often exclude it.
logistics.weather: Pindus afternoon convection is the defining hazard — clear mornings turn to lightning on the treeless Tymfi karst from about 14:00 in June and September. Autumn cold fronts off the Ionian can flood the gorge bed within a day.
logistics.bookingWindows: **Astraka refuge** books by phone/email and fills on summer weekends and Greek holidays — 2–4 weeks ahead, more for August. It opens around **22 May** and closes in October; outside that only the unstaffed winter room, with no water. Aristi Mountain Resort goes 2–3 months ahead for late September.
logistics.money: Euro. Hotels and larger tavernas take cards; **the refuge, kafeneia and small tavernas are frequently cash-only**. Carry €150–€200 from Ioannina — Zagori ATMs are limited to Tsepelovo and Papingo and run dry at weekends. Round up or leave 5–10%.
logistics.transportRules: A rental car is non-negotiable; buses run once or twice daily at best. Egnatia Odos from Ioannina is tolled (a few euros per gate). Inter-village roads are narrow, unlit and full of sheep — do not plan fast night driving.
logistics.permits: Vikos–Aoos National Park has **no entry fee** and needs no permit to run. Wild camping in the core zone is prohibited. Drones need park permission. Open fires are banned May–October.
logistics.health: Village taps and named springs are potable; treat lake and standing water. **Ticks** in beech leaf litter May–July — check nightly. Nose-horned vipers live on sunny limestone; make noise on rock ledges. Sheepdogs guarding flocks on the plateau are serious — stop, don't run, wait for the shepherd.

proTips: **Run the gorge north-to-south.** Almost everyone starts at Monodendri; start at Vikos village and you meet the crowd head-on for twenty minutes then have empty trail, and the brutal 450 m Monodendri climb becomes a known quantity at the end rather than a surprise descent on tired ankles.
**Sleep at the refuge mid-week.** Astraka fills with Greek groups Friday and Saturday; a Tuesday night can mean fifteen people in a 51-bed hut.
**Pre-position water for the Tymfi descent.** Stash a litre at the Antalki junction on the way up in July–September; the last 700 m of descent in afternoon sun is where people cook.
**Use the refuge as a weather oracle.** Call the hut the day before your ridge day — the guardian's read on plateau cloudbase beats any app.
**Do the Vradeto Steps at 18:30.** The Mezaria ravine faces west, the light on the stone is extraordinary, and the Beloi coach parties are long gone.
**Carry the Anavasi paper sheet anyway.** Above the Astraka col the karst is featureless and a phone inside a rain shell is a liability.
**Book the Voidomatis raft for a rest-day morning.** The river is shaded until midday at 8–10 °C — accidental cold-water recovery after the Astraka block.

raw.Signature routes: (1) **Vikos Gorge traverse, Monodendri→Vikos village**: 12.8 km, 320 m up / 690 m down, mid-pack 2 h 15–3 h. (2) **Astraka refuge & Drakolimni from Mikro Papingo**: 15.5 km, 1,290 m D+, 3 h 15–4 h 15. (3) **Astraka summit (2,436 m) via the col and Lapatos**: 19 km, 1,600 m D+, 4 h 30–6 h. (4) **Vradeto Steps + Beloi rim loop from Kapesovo**: 11 km, 520 m D+, 1 h 30–2 h. (5) **Kalderimi link Kipoi–Koukouli–Dilofo–Vitsa**: 14 km, 600 m D+, 1 h 45–2 h 30.
raw.Technicality (ITRA-style 1–5; 1 = fire r: Gorge floor **3–4** (loose cobble, wet slab, two boulder-hop crossings); Tymfi ascent **3**; Astraka summit ridge **4**, with 20–30 m of easy exposed scrambling below the summit block; village kalderimia **2**, though polished flagstone is genuinely slick when damp. SAC equivalents: gorge T2–T3, Astraka T3.
raw.Terrain split, week average: ~45% limestone cobble and rock step, ~20% karst pavement and scree above 1,800 m, ~20% beech and black-pine singletrack with deep leaf litter, ~10% engineered kalderimi flagstone, ~5% asphalt connectors. Bring 4 mm+ lugs and a rock plate — Tymfi karst destroys soft midsoles.
raw.Waymarking: Gorge and Tymfi approaches carry **O3** (Greek national long-distance path) in red/white paint plus wooden Zagori NP posts timed in hours. Village links use yellow diamonds. Above the treeline, cairns matter more than paint.
raw.Water refill points and month reliabilit: *Voidomatis springs* at Klima below Vikos village — permanent, 8 °C, the most reliable source in Epirus. *Astraka refuge* — piped spring, reliable while staffed (from ~22 May), dry when the hut is shut. *Drakolimni* — lake water, filter or treat. *Mikro/Megalo Papingo, Kipoi, Koukouli, Vradeto, Kapesovo, Tsepelovo* village fountains — year-round. *Antalki/Trafos spring* on the Papingo ascent — reliable May–June, often dry August–September. Assume **nothing between Mikro Papingo and the refuge after mid-July**.
raw.Navigation: Anavasi 1:25,000 sheets 6.1 (Zagori–Vikos–Aoos) and 6.11 (Tymfi); GPX from the Anavasi topo app and Wikiloc ("O3 Vikos"). **Zero signal on the gorge floor for ~9 km** between Monodendri and the springs, patchy on the north Tymfi plateau. Bail-outs: from the gorge, side paths to Vikos village and the Klidonia road bridge; from Tymfi, only the refuge and the Papingo descent — the Tsepelovo side is a 4 h+ commitment.
raw.Recovery and heat management: Day 5 is a true low day (under 8 km, flat). Gorge days start by 07:00 — the east rim shades the floor to about 10:00, then it becomes an oven. Tymfi days start 06:30 to clear the treeless plateau before the 14:00–16:00 Pindus convective build-up. High point 2,497 m (Gamila); no acclimatisation needed, but the refuge night is a useful sleep-high dose.

sources.verified: Astraka refuge's official site confirms 1,950 m, 51 beds and a stated 2026 opening of 22 May; Vikos–Aoos National Park charges no entry fee; IOA as base airport; Greece EU roaming.
sources.confidenceNotes: Re-verify (a) **Astraka refuge exact opening/closing dates and current nightly and half-board prices**, set year to year by the guardian; (b) **spring reliability at Antalki/Trafos**, which tracks the winter snowpack — confirm with the refuge in the booking month; (c) **taverna trading status and shoulder-season opening days** for Sterna, Kanela kai Garyfallo and Kalliopi; (d) **accommodation price bands**, especially Aristi Mountain Resort; (e) **O3 paint condition and flood damage on the gorge floor** — the Voidomatis bed reshapes in flood years and crossings move.
